articles.title: Canada extends 150,000 international student arrivals target to 2029
articles.summary: Canada has extended its annual target of 150,000 new international student arrivals through 2029. This target was originally established in last year’s immigration plan and will remain unchanged for the extended period.
articles.insight:
Canada’s extension of its 150,000 annual international student intake target to 2029 signals sustained policy-level commitment to international education, potentially reinforcing perceptions of Canada as a stable, accessible destination—though actual demand shifts depend on concurrent factors like visa processing times, post-study work rights, and global economic conditions.  
Admissions teams should monitor Canadian visa approval rates, provincial study permit restrictions, and comparative affordability data across key source markets, while reviewing their own value propositions around career outcomes and immigration pathways to ensure competitive differentiation remains clear and credible.

articles.title: RMIT spends 183 billion VND in scholarships for 2027
articles.summary: RMIT Vietnam University has allocated 183 billion VND for scholarships in 2027. The funding supports 156 scholarships across undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral programs.
articles.insight:
RMIT Vietnam’s significant 2027 scholarship investment signals growing regional capacity to retain high-achieving Southeast Asian students, potentially moderating outbound demand for Western degrees—though direct impact on US/UK/AU/NZ enrolments remains uncertain without data on overlap in target demographics or program competitiveness.  
Admissions teams should monitor Vietnamese and broader ASEAN application trends, scholarship uptake rates, and graduate outcomes from RMIT’s expanded offerings, while assessing whether their own financial aid strategies remain competitive for academically strong candidates from these markets.

articles.title: Why the Philippines’ new TNE strategy could make it South East Asia’s partnership hotspot
articles.summary: The Philippines’ new transnational education (TNE) strategy is positioned to make it a partnership hotspot in Southeast Asia due to its large youth population, extensive higher education system, and strong government support. Higher education leaders cited these factors as key enablers for expanding TNE partnerships, according to The PIE News.
articles.insight:
The Philippines’ new TNE strategy may gradually shift regional student mobility patterns, as strengthened local partnerships could delay or divert some Southeast Asian students from traditional Anglophone destinations—though direct impact on enrolment volumes remains uncertain and likely medium-term.  
Admissions teams should monitor Philippine TNE programme launches, bilateral MOUs, and enrolment data from key feeder countries like Vietnam and Indonesia to assess whether rising domestic capacity begins influencing application trends or scholarship preferences.

articles.title: ‘Treated differently’: foreign students in India confront everyday discrimination
articles.summary: International students in India report experiencing everyday discrimination, including being stereotyped as drug users based on their skin colour. They also face unequal treatment at university gates and other settings outside the classroom.
articles.insight:
This news may indirectly influence student demand from regions where India is a key competitor for outbound students—such as Nigeria, Bangladesh, or Nepal—as prospective applicants weigh perceptions of safety, inclusion, and everyday equity in alternative destinations. While not yet evidence of shifting enrolment trends, it adds context to growing global scrutiny of host-country social climates.  
Admissions teams should monitor sentiment shifts in priority source markets via social listening and agent feedback, particularly around narratives linking destination countries with racial equity, campus safety, and lived student experience—not just academic or visa policy factors.
